think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 39-year-old woman presented with an 18-month history of chronic intermittent colicky right upper quadrant abdominal pain and nausea, simulating chronic cholecystitis or symptomatic cholelithiasis. Plain abdominal radiography demonstrated a calcified opacity at L2–L3. Primary echinococcosis localized to the gallbladder wall without liver parenchymal cysts is an exceptional clinical entity (under 1% of hydatid cases), and was preoperatively misidentified on ultrasound and CT as a primary liver hydatid cyst compressing the gallbladder.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage ends following history of chronic colicky RUQ pain, physical exam showing mild RUQ tenderness without jaundice, normal CBC, liver and renal function panels, normal chest x-ray, and abdominal radiograph showing an L2–L3 calcified opacity, immediately prior to cross-sectional imaging (ultrasound, CT) and exploratory laparotomy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Chronic cholelithiasis / biliary colic / peptic ulcer disease was initially managed by primary care with antispasmodics, H2-blockers, and antibiotics without benefit. Primary calcified hepatic hydatid cyst invading or displacing the gallbladder was the preoperative cross-sectional imaging consensus, but intraoperative exploration and pathology revealed the cyst wall originated entirely within the gallbladder submucosa.
case_prompt:
A 39-year-old Kosovan Albanian woman was referred to an abdominal surgery service for an 18-month history of chronic, intermittently colicky pain in the right upper quadrant, often accompanied by nausea. There was no history of fever, chills, pruritus, or jaundice. She had been managed medically by her primary care physician with antispasmodic agents, H2 receptor blockers, and empirical antibiotics without clinical resolution.

On admission, physical examination revealed mild tenderness upon palpation in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen without guarding or rebound tenderness. Murphy's sign was negative. The remainder of the abdominal and systemic examination was unremarkable, and sclerae were anicteric.

Triage laboratory investigations, including complete blood count, serum renal panel, and liver function tests, were within normal limits. Chest radiography showed normal cardiopulmonary anatomy without infiltrates or diaphragmatic elevation. A plain abdominal radiograph demonstrated a well-defined calcified opacity projected at the level of the L2–L3 vertebrae in the right upper quadrant.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Chronic cholecystitis / Biliary colic / Peptic disease
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to 18 months of chronic postprandial colicky right upper quadrant pain and nausea; unresponsive to medical therapy with antispasmodics and H2 blockers, and ruled out by discovery of a large calcified parasitic mass.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: She had been treated by her primary care physician with antispasmodics, H2 receptor blockers and antibiotics, without resolution.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary calcified hepatic hydatid cyst with secondary gallbladder compression
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Preoperatively diagnosed by ultrasound and computed tomography as a primary liver parenchymal cyst extrinsic to the gallbladder; disproven intraoperatively when surgical dissection demonstrated origin directly within the gallbladder wall.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The diagnosis, supported by ultrasound and computed tomography, was a calcified hydatid cyst of the liver with involvement and deformation of the gallbladder; the architecture and the size of biliary ducts were normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Right subcostal laparotomy revealed a 7 x 5 cm calcified hydatid cyst arising entirely submucosally within the fundus and body of the gallbladder with severe luminal reduction, confirmed on definitive histopathologic evaluation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The histopathology confirmed the presence of calcified hydatid cyst of the gallbladder (Figure 4).

editor_comments: A rare presentation of primary gallbladder echinococcosis growing strictly within the submucosal layer of the fundus and body, causing chronic biliary colic and mimicking a calcified liver parenchymal cyst on preoperative imaging.
